governing_thought: A 5-day close is a re-sequencing problem first: 7 days out, USD 1.6M NPV, 12 to 15 months.

slides.title: A 5-day close is a re‑sequencing problem first
slides.subtitle: 7 days out, USD 1.6M NPV, 12 to 15 months. Figures other than days to close are illustrative.

placeholders.13: CFO board pack: month-end close, 12 to 5 days

slides.notes: Client figures other than days to close are illustrative assumptions.

slides.title: The bank can close in 5 days, and a third of the gain needs no software

placeholders.13: The board approves a capacity plan, not a date. Below about 24% effort released, the case destroys value [S06].

bullets: **7 days removed by six levers.** Today's 12 days is in the APQC bottom quartile; the median is 6.5 and the top quartile 4 [S02].
**About 2.5 days need no software.** They come from re-sequencing bank-specific tasks (ECL, IPV, FTP) off the legal-entity close path: a policy and auditor decision, not a spend decision.
**Base case:** USD 3.5M investment, NPV USD 1.58M, IRR 22.95%, payback 2.94 years [S06].
slides.source: Source: APQC via VOLT [S02]; VOLT value-case engine [S06]; client intake [S01].
slides.notes: The whole argument on one page. The capacity plan is the condition for value.

slides.title: Every board KPI falls by 40% or more; days to close is the headline
bullets: Only days to close is measured today; the other three are baseline assumptions pending a two-close time survey.
slides.source: Source: client intake [S01]; benchmark [S02]; the other three KPIs are [ASSUMPTION]. Today values = target + stated change.
slides.notes: Lead with days to close; it is the only measured KPI.

slides.title: At 12 days the close is 5.5 days behind the median; close, technology and data are weakest

11: **High priority:** close and consolidation, finance technology, data and reporting, each 2.0 against a target of 4.0.
**Medium:** controls, operating model, change readiness. **Low:** planning and forecasting.

slides.source: Source: VOLT maturity model [S05], scored on assumed evidence; APQC days to close [S02].
slides.notes: Maturity scores are on a 1 to 5 scale.

slides.title: Wrong sequencing and manual matching each cause 36% of the gap

rows: ECL, IPV and FTP sit on the close path

slides.source: Source: [Verify]. Estimated from bank close patterns; to be confirmed by a critical-path map.
slides.notes: The first two causes are 5 of the 7 days.

slides.title: Six levers take the close from 12 days to 5

11: **Policy levers give 3 days in two quarters;** tooling levers give the other 4.
**ECL and valuations pre-close** is the largest single lever: -2 days.

slides.source: Source: [ESTIMATE] lever sizing; baseline [S01]; benchmark [S02]. Lever names completed from the source deck's wording (see notes).
slides.notes: Business days. Full lever names: ECL and valuations pre-close; sub-ledger feeds; risk-tiered reconciliations; intercompany; FTP off the close path; single consolidation run. Five were cut off in the source chart and are completed from the deck's own wording.

slides.title: Reconciliation releases 900 of the 2,550 hours per close, more than any other phase

11: **6,000 to 3,450 hours,** a 42% fall, equal to about 17 FTE.
**Reconciliation:** 1,500 accounts at 1.2 h today; tiered: 540 + 240 + 120 = 900 h.
Two phases are combined: the source chart did not label them separately after the change.

slides.source: Source: [ASSUMPTION] illustrative baseline. Released = before minus after, per phase, from the source chart.
slides.notes: Before: sub-ledger 900, reconciliation 1,800, journals 1,200, reporting 800, intercompany and one further phase 1,300. After: 500, 900, 700, 550, 800.

slides.title: The reds cluster on Bank OpCo accruals, ECL and reconciliations, which sit on the critical path

11: Leasing reporting can wait for wave 2.
R red, A amber, G green.

slides.source: Source: [ASSUMPTION]. Illustrative entity set; to be validated in controller interviews.

slides.title: In the target close, judgement happens before D1 and only six steps sit on the critical path

cells.heading: D2  ECL true-up
bullets: ECL true-up in the ECL engine
**Before D1:** close calendar and cut-off (D-2), ECL run on D-2 balances (D-1, flagged with a warning in the source), IC agreement deadline (D-1).
**Off the critical path:** valuations and IPV exceptions (D1), high-risk recs certified (D2), automated flux and board pack, regulatory data lock (D4).
slides.source: Source: [ESTIMATE] target design; systems are generic until the platform is confirmed.
slides.notes: Thirteen steps in total across six teams, D-2 to D5; six are on the critical path.

slides.title: Option B, a close layer on the current GL, scores 4.35 and leads at every weighting tested
slides.source: Source: [ASSUMPTION] weights and scores; [ESTIMATE] costs, pending vendor quotes. A wins below USD 1.5M or if the GL is replaced within 24 months; C wins if the GL is out of support.

slides.title: USD 1.6M base NPV, but effort released swings it by about USD 4.9M

cells.heading: USD 1.58M
bullets: **Base NPV** at 30% effort released (18 FTE) and USD 3.5M investment: IRR 22.95%, payback 2.94 years.
**Low case** (20%, USD 5.0M): NPV -2.39M, IRR -9.87%, payback not reached.
**High case** (40%, USD 2.5M): NPV 5.05M, IRR 60.94%, payback 1.73 years.

slides.source: Source: VOLT value-case engine [S06]. Inputs: 60 FTE, USD 120k loaded cost, USD 0.6M run cost a year, 9% discount rate, 5 years, 2-year ramp.
slides.notes: Chart: one-at-a-time NPV sensitivity, USD M.

slides.notes: Quick wins take the close to about 9 days in Q1.

slides.title: Two risks decide success: auditor acceptance of the design, and redeploying the freed capacity

rows: Walkthrough 1-2 quarters before go-live; hard close at quarter-end
Capacity not redeployed, so NPV turns negative
Re-run threshold; daily report of loans moving into arrears
Regulatory returns stop reconciling to the ledger
Profile 3 months of data before the build

slides.notes: The first two rows decide the case.

slides.title: Three decisions in the next 30 days
bullets: **Re-sequence first.** About 2.5 days come from moving ECL, IPV and FTP off the close path, with no software.
**Choose Option B,** a close layer on the current GL: 4.35, ahead at every weighting tested.
**Fund capacity, not a date.** Below about 24% effort released the case destroys value.

11: Approve soft-close principles for an auditor walkthrough (CFO).
Commit to redeploying about 18 FTE of capacity, the condition for a positive NPV (CFO and HR).
Fund Option B discovery and tool selection (CFO and CIO).

slides.source: Source: [ESTIMATE]. Research depth: STANDARD. Only days to close is client data [S01].
